newsitem.title: USA: Khouri to leave Michigan deputy treasurer post.
newsitem.headline: Khouri to leave Michigan deputy treasurer post.

text.p: Nick Khouri will leave his job as Michigan's chief deputy treasurer in mid-January, according to a news release from the state's Department of Treasury.
Khouri, who has been chief deputy since the start of Gov. John Engler's administration in January 1991, will spend the winter consulting with the government of Guam, according to the release.
In the spring, Khouri will join the staff of Public Sector Consultants, a Lansing, Mich.-based public policy organization.
During his tenure with state government, Khouri was responsible for much of the state's bond issuance.
Neither Khouri nor Michigan Treasurer Doug Roberts were available Thursday to comment on Khouri's departure, which was announced on Monday.
The news release quoted Roberts as saying he would miss Khouri's "top-notch counsel and considerable knowledge, especially in the fields of tax law, municipal bonding and finance."
According to the release, Khouri said he had worked with Roberts for nearly a decade that that he would miss his "guidance and support."
